name: Chin tuck
why: Wakes up the deep muscles at the front of your neck that hold your head balanced over your shoulders. After long hours at a screen the head drifts forward and these muscles switch off, which loads the back of the neck.
setup: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Look straight ahead with your chin level.
mistakes: Tipping the chin down to the chest instead of sliding the head back
Pushing so hard that the neck strains
feel: A gentle stretch at the base of your skull and light effort at the front of your neck.
stopIf: Pain spreads into your arm, or you feel dizzy, tingly or numb.

name: Upper trapezius stretch
why: Eases tightness along the side of the neck and top of the shoulder, where tension builds up with stress, desk work and carrying bags.
setup: Sit tall and hold the side of the chair seat with your right hand to keep that shoulder down.
Slowly tilt your left ear towards your left shoulder.
Optional: rest your left hand on your head for a little extra weight. Don't pull.
mistakes: Letting the stretched-side shoulder creep up
Turning the head instead of tilting it
feel: A stretch along the side of the neck into the top of the shoulder, on the side away from the tilt.
stopIf: Pain or tingling travels down your arm, or you feel dizzy.
